10: export const EntirePlugin: Plugin = async ({ directory }) => {
11:   // Track seen user messages to fire turn-start only once per message
12:   const seenUserMessages = new Set<string>()
13:   // Track current session ID for message events (which don't include sessionID)
14:   let currentSessionID: string | null = null
15:   // Track the model used by the most recent assistant message
16:   let currentModel: string | null = null
17:   // In-memory store for message metadata (role, tokens, etc.)
18:   const messageStore = new Map<string, any>()
19:   // One-time model-context injection captured from the turn-start hook's stdout,
20:   // applied on the next LLM call via experimental.chat.system.transform.
21:   let pendingInjection: string | null = null
22: 
23:   /**
24:    * Build the shell command for a hook invocation.
25:    * Uses sh -c so the command is guarded by a `command -v` probe: when the
26:    * entire binary is not on PATH the hook exits 0 rather than failing the
27:    * surrounding OpenCode operation.
28:    */
29:   function hookCmd(hookName: string): string[] {
30:     return ["sh", "-c", `if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi; exec entire hooks opencode ${hookName}`]
31:   }
32: 
33:   /**
34:    * Pipe JSON payload to an entire hooks command (async).
35:    * Errors are logged but never thrown — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode.
36:    */
37:   async function callHook(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
38:     try {
39:       const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
40:       const [cmd, ...args] = hookCmd(hookName)
41:       await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
42:         const proc = spawn(cmd, args, {
43:           cwd: directory,
44:           stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "ignore"],
45:         })
46:         proc.on("error", () => resolve())
47:         proc.on("close", () => resolve())
48:         proc.stdin?.end(json + "\n")
49:       })
50:     } catch {
51:       // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
52:     }
53:   }
54: 
55:   /**
56:    * Synchronous variant for hooks that must complete before subsequent agent work
57:    * or process exit. `turn-start` must finish initializing session state before a
58:    * fast mid-turn commit can hit git hooks, and `turn-end` / `session-end` must
59:    * finish before `opencode run` tears down its event loop.
60:    */
61:   function callHookSync(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
62:     try {
63:       const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
64:       const [cmd, ...args] = hookCmd(hookName)
65:       spawnSync(cmd, args, {
66:         cwd: directory,
67:         input: json + "\n",
68:         stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "ignore"],
69:       })
70:     } catch {
71:       // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
72:     }
73:   }

76:   // ({"inject_context":"..."}) and returns the text to inject, or null.
77:   function parseInjectedContext(stdout: string): string | null {
78:     if (!stdout) return null
79:     for (const line of stdout.split("\n")) {
80:       const trimmed = line.trim()
81:       if (!trimmed.startsWith("{")) continue
82:       try {
83:         const parsed = JSON.parse(trimmed) as { inject_context?: unknown }
84:         if (typeof parsed.inject_context === "string" && parsed.inject_context.length > 0) {
85:           return parsed.inject_context
86:         }
87:       } catch {
88:         // not our envelope — ignore
89:       }
90:     }
91:     return null
92:   }
93: 
94:   // fireTurnStart fires turn-start synchronously (state must be ready before
95:   // mid-turn commits) and stashes any model-context injection emitted on stdout
96:   // for experimental.chat.system.transform to apply. Entire emits the injection
97:   // at most once per session, so pendingInjection is set on the first turn only.

# Skill: browser-automation # browser-automation Closes the edit → run → **look at it** → fix loop that otherwise requires the user to describe what is on their screen. ## Usage ```bash node /browser.mjs [options] ``` `` is the folder you just read this file from — `browser.mjs` sits beside it. Use that path literally rather than guessing at a home directory. | option | meaning | |---|---| | `--snapshot` | list every interactive element with a clickable ref (add `--full` for the whole accessibility tree) | | `--wait ` | block until the selector appears (default: DOM ready) | | `--eval ` | run an expression in the page, print the JSON result | | `--script ` | drive a sequence — see **Scripting** below | | `--screenshot

` | write a PNG — read it afterwards to look at it | | `--timeout ` | navigation timeout, default 30000 | | `--session ` | keep ONE page alive across calls — see **Sessions** below | | `--close` | with `--session `, tear that session's browser down | ## Driving by ref, not by selector `--snapshot` returns the page's interactive elements, each with a ref: ``` @e5 button "Audit my code" @e9 button "Select your model" [haspopup=menu] @e10 button "Manual" [haspopup=menu] @e11 button "Send" [disabled] ``` Click `@e10` and you get what the page says is there — no selector to author from a DOM you cannot see. This matters most for **icon-only buttons**, which have no accessible name at all: `getByRole('button', {name: …})` cannot find them, and they show up here as `@e1 button [haspopup=dialog]`. A ref is stamped into the page, so it dies on navigation or a re-render. **Re-snapshot after anything that changes the page** — the refs renumber, and a stale one matches nothing. `--full` returns the accessibility tree instead (headings, text, links). Use refs to *act*, `--full` to *read*. ## Scripting a sequence `--script` runs a file that default-exports `async (page, ui) => result`. **`page` is a Playwright `Page`** (the driver is patchright, a Playwright fork), so use the Playwright API — `page.locator`, `page.getByRole`, `page.getByText`, `page.waitForFunction`, `page.evaluate`. It is NOT Puppeteer: `page.$` and friends mostly work, but `getByRole` and `locator` do not exist there, so code written against Puppeteer will fail in confusing ways. **`ui` is the ref helper**, and is usually the shorter path: | call | does | |---|---| | `await ui.snapshot()` | the ref listing above, as a string | | `await ui.snapshot({full: true})` | the accessibility tree instead | | `await ui.click('@e7')` | click that element | | `await ui.fill('@e3', 'text')` | fill an input | | `await ui.text('@e5')` | its inner text | | `ui.ref('@e5')` | the raw locator, for anything else | Whatever you return is printed as JSON. The runner owns the browser, the console/network capture and the teardown; the script only drives and asserts. ```js // qa.mjs — node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --script ./qa.mjs export default async function run(page, ui) { // Look at what is there before deciding what to click. const before = await ui.snapshot() const signIn = before.match(/@(e\d+) button "Sign in"/)?.[1] if (!signIn) return { error: 'no sign-in button', snapshot: before } await ui.click(signIn) await page.waitForTimeout(500) // The page changed, so the old refs are gone — snapshot again. const after = await ui.snapshot() return { opened: after.includes('textbox'), after } } ``` Navigation to the URL argument has already happened before your function runs. You can navigate further with `page.goto(...)`. ## Read the text before the pixels `--screenshot` writes a PNG and **you can read it** — a read of an image returns the picture. If it comes back as `[binary file: png …]` this host has no image path; say so rather than guessing at what rendered. Even so, reach for text first. It is not just cheaper — it is more precise: - `--snapshot` — every interactive element, with refs - `--snapshot --full` — the accessibility tree: headings, text, links - `--eval "…"` — ask the DOM a direct question - the console/network report, which catches most breakage for almost nothing A screenshot costs tens of thousands of tokens and answers "does this look right", which is a narrower question than it seems. Use it for layout and visual regressions, and use the tree for everything about structure, content and state. ## Interpreting the report - `console.error` / uncaught exceptions → almost always a real bug. - `requests failed` → a 404 on a JS chunk usually means a stale build is being served; a 500 means the server, not the page. - `title` empty and `bodyChars` near zero → the app did not mount at all. Check the console section first, not the DOM. ## Examples ```bash # Did my change render? node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 # Assert something specific about the DOM node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 \ --eval "document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=row]').length" # Wait for a late-mounting element before judging the page node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --wait "[data-testid=grid]" ``` ## Gotchas found by using this - **Keep the trailing slash** on a path-prefixed app. `http://host/app` and `http://host/app/` resolve relative asset URLs differently, and without it a page can return HTTP 200 with `bodyChars 0` and never mount. An app that 200s but renders nothing is usually this, not a crash. - **A failing request is not automatically a bug.** Apps routinely probe for optional local services that are simply not running. Check whether the dependency is meant to exist before reporting it. - **Never assert on text your own input put on the page.** A check for "console error" matches the prompt you just typed into the app as readily as the thing you were looking for, and the test passes while proving nothing. Match only strings that can come from the system under test. - **Wait for content, not for a fixed delay.** A client-rendered app that is merely slow is indistinguishable from one that is broken unless you actually wait for something to appear. - **Prefer a ref over a selector.** A selector that silently matches nothing and an element that is genuinely absent produce the same failure, and you cannot tell them apart without looking. `--snapshot` first, then act on what it listed. When a check still says something is missing, use `--snapshot --full` to read the tree before reporting it, and screenshot if the question is genuinely visual. - Third-party analytics failures are filtered out; they are noise, not signal. ## One run, one browser (the default) By default each invocation launches a browser, does the work, and closes it. Cookies, logins and page state do **not** survive to the next invocation, so a short sequence should happen inside a single `--script` run rather than across several calls. This is the right default: most QA is "load this, tell me what broke." ## Sessions — keep one page alive across calls When you need to *think between steps* — drive a form, read the result, decide the next action, drive again — a single `--script` can't help, because you don't know step 3 until you've seen step 2. Use `--session `: the browser stays alive between separate invocations and every call reconnects to the **same page** it left open. ```bash # Step 1: open the app in a named session, set something up node /browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --session qa1 --snapshot # Step 2: NO url — act on the page the session already has open node /browser.mjs --session qa1 --eval "document.querySelector('#total').innerText" # Step 3: re-navigate within the same session if you want, or keep acting node /browser.mjs --session qa1 --script ./next-step.mjs # When done — always tear it down, or the browser stays running node /browser.mjs --session qa1 --close ``` Rules: - **Omit the url** on follow-up calls to act on the current page; **pass a url** to navigate the session's page somewhere new. - Refs from `--snapshot` still die on navigation/re-render — re-snapshot after anything that changes the page, same as one-shot mode. - **Always `--close` when finished.** The browser is detached and outlives the call by design; without `--close` it keeps running until the machine reboots. - Sessions are headless and use a throwaway profile per id under `~/.codegpt/ab-sessions/` — never the user's real browser or cookies. ## Notes - Resolves `patchright` from an installed CodeGPT extension, then a dev checkout, then a global copy — so it normally needs no install of its own. If none is found it says what it looked for. - Headless. It never touches the user's real browser profile or cookies. 1: ---
2: title: useParams
3: description: API Reference for the useParams hook.
4: ---
5: 
6: `useParams` is a **Client Component** hook that lets you read a route's [dynamic params](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) filled in by the current URL.
7: 
8: ```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
9: 'use client'
10: 
11: import { useParams } from 'next/navigation'
12: 
13: export default function ExampleClientComponent() {
14:   const params = useParams<{ tag: string; item: string }>()
15: 
16:   // Route -> /shop/[tag]/[item]
17:   // URL -> /shop/shoes/nike-air-max-97
18:   // `params` -> { tag: 'shoes', item: 'nike-air-max-97' }
19:   console.log(params)
20: 
21:   return '...'
22: }
23: ```
24: 
25: ```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
26: 'use client'
27: 
28: import { useParams } from 'next/navigation'
29: 
30: export default function ExampleClientComponent() {
31:   const params = useParams()
32: 
33:   // Route -> /shop/[tag]/[item]
34:   // URL -> /shop/shoes/nike-air-max-97
35:   // `params` -> { tag: 'shoes', item: 'nike-air-max-97' }
36:   console.log(params)
37: 
38:   return '...'
39: }
40: ```
41: 
42: ## Parameters
43: 
44: ```tsx
45: const params = useParams()
46: ```
47: 
48: `useParams` does not take any parameters.
49: 
50: ## Returns
51: 
52: `useParams` returns an object containing the current route's filled in [dynamic parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes).
53: 
54: - Each property in the object is an active dynamic segment.
55: - The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what the segment is filled in with.
56: - The properties value will either be a `string` or array of `string`'s depending on the [type of dynamic segment](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes).
57: - If the route contains no dynamic parameters, `useParams` returns an empty object.
58: - If used in Pages Router, `useParams` will return `null` on the initial render and updates with properties following the rules above once the router is ready.
59: 
60: For example:
61: 
62: | Route                           | URL         | `useParams()`             |
63: | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
64: | `app/shop/page.js`              | `/shop`     | `{}`                      |
65: | `app/shop/[slug]/page.js`       | `/shop/1`   | `{ slug: '1' }`           |
66: | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `{ tag: '1', item: '2' }` |
67: | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js`    | `/shop/1/2` | `{ slug: ['1', '2'] }`    |
68: 
69: ## Behavior
70: 
71: ### Cache Components
72: 
73: When [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, `useParams` may require a [`Suspense`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary. This depends on whether the params can be resolved during prerendering.
74: 
75: - **Static routes and routes with [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)**: every dynamic param is known at build time. `useParams` resolves on the server and no `Suspense` boundary is required.
76: - **Routes with dynamic params not covered by `generateStaticParams`**: the param is not known until request time. `useParams` suspends. Wrap the component (or a parent) in a `Suspense` boundary so its fallback can be rendered during prerendering; otherwise, the build fails.
77: 
78: See [Next.js encountered URL data in a Client Component outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-client-hook) for full fix options and trade-offs.
79: 
80: ## Version History
81: 
82: | Version   | Changes                 |
83: | --------- | ----------------------- |
84: | `v13.3.0` | `useParams` introduced. |

(End of file - total 84 lines)

13: 
14: You can use the `metadata` object or the `generateMetadata` function to define metadata.
15: 
16: ## The `metadata` object
17: 
18: To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) from a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
19: 
20: ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
21: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
22: 
23: export const metadata: Metadata = {
24:   title: '...',
25:   description: '...',
26: }
27: 
28: export default function Page() {}
29: ```
30: 
31: ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
32: export const metadata = {
33:   title: '...',
34:   description: '...',
35: }
36: 
37: export default function Page() {}
38: ```
39: 
40: > See the [Metadata Fields](#metadata-fields) for a complete list of supported options.
41: 
42: ## `generateMetadata` function
43: 
44: Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
45: 
46: Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.
47: 
48: Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.
49: 
50: ```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
51: import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
52: 
53: type Props = {
54:   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
55:   searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
56: }
57: 
58: export async function generateMetadata(
59:   { params, searchParams }: Props,
60:   parent: ResolvingMetadata
61: ): Promise<Metadata> {
62:   // read route params
63:   const { id } = await params
64: 
65:   // fetch data
66:   const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
67: 
68:   // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
69:   const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
70: 
71:   return {
72:     title: product.title,
73:     openGraph: {
74:       images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
75:     },
76:   }
77: }
78: 
79: export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
80: ```
81: 
82: ```jsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.js" switcher
83: export async function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }, parent) {
84:   // read route params
85:   const { id } = await params
86: 
87:   // fetch data
88:   const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
89: 
90:   // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
91:   const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
92: 
93:   return {
94:     title: product.title,
95:     openGraph: {
96:       images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
97:     },
98:   }
99: }
100: 
101: export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) {}
102: ```
103: 
104: For type completion of `params` and `searchParams`, you can type the first argument with [`PageProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`LayoutProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) for pages and layouts respectively.
105: 
106: > **Good to know**:
107: >
108: > - Metadata can be added to `layout.js` and `page.js` files.
109: > - Next.js will automatically resolve the metadata, and create the relevant `<head>` tags for the page.
110: > - The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are **only supported in Server Components**.
111: > - You cannot export both the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function from the same route segment.
112: > - `fetch` requests inside `generateMetadata` are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components.
113: > - React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
114: > - [File-based metadata](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) has the higher priority and will override the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function.
115: 
116: ## Why `generateMetadata` is Server Component only
117: 
118: `generateMetadata` and the `metadata` export are only supported in Server Components because metadata must be resolved on the server before the page component is rendered. This allows Next.js to include the metadata in the initial HTML response.
119: 
120: If you need to use Client Component features, keep your `page.tsx` as a Server Component and move the Client Component logic to a separate file:
121: 
122: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
123: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
124: import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
125: 
126: export const metadata: Metadata = {
127:   title: 'My Page',
128: }
129: 
130: export default function Page() {
131:   return <InteractiveComponent />
132: }
133: ```
134: 
135: ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
136: import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
137: 
138: export const metadata = {
139:   title: 'My Page',
140: }
141: 
142: export default function Page() {
143:   return <InteractiveComponent />
144: }
145: ```
146: 
147: ```tsx filename="app/interactive-component.tsx" switcher
148: 'use client'
149: 
150: export function InteractiveComponent() {
151:   // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
152: }
153: ```
154: 
155: ```jsx filename="app/interactive-component.js" switcher
156: 'use client'
157: 
158: export function InteractiveComponent() {
159:   // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
160: }
161: ```
162: 
163: ## Reference
164: 
165: ### Parameters
166: 
167: `generateMetadata` function accepts the following parameters:
168: 
169: - `props` - An object containing the parameters of the current route:
170:   - `params` - An object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to the segment `generateMetadata` is called from. Examples:
171: 
172:     | Route                           | URL         | `params`                  |
173:     | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
174:     | `app/shop/[slug]/page.js`       | `/shop/1`   | `{ slug: '1' }`           |
175:     | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `{ tag: '1', item: '2' }` |
176:     | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js`    | `/shop/1/2` | `{ slug: ['1', '2'] }`    |
177: 
178:   - `searchParams` - An object containing the current URL's [search params](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Learn/Common_questions/What_is_a_URL#parameters). Examples:
179: 
180:     | URL             | `searchParams`       |
181:     | --------------- | -------------------- |
182:     | `/shop?a=1`     | `{ a: '1' }`         |
183:     | `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `{ a: '1', b: '2' }` |
184:     | `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `{ a: ['1', '2'] }`  |
185: 
186: - `parent` - A promise of the resolved metadata from parent route segments.
187: 
188: ### Returns
189: 
190: `generateMetadata` should return a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) containing one or more metadata fields.
191: 
192: > **Good to know**:
193: >
194: > - If metadata doesn't depend on request information, it should be defined using the static [`metadata` object](#the-metadata-object) rather than `generateMetadata`.
195: > - `fetch` requests are automatically memoized for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
196: > - `searchParams` are only available in `page.js` segments.
197: > - The [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) and [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) Next.js methods can also be used inside `generateMetadata`.
198: 
199: ### Metadata Fields
200: 
201: The following fields are supported:
202: 
203: #### `title`
204: 
205: The `title` attribute is used to set the title of the document. It can be defined as a simple [string](#string) or an optional [template object](#template).
206: 
207: ##### String
208: 
209: ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
210: export const metadata = {
211:   title: 'Next.js',
212: }
213: ```
214: 
215: ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
216: <title>Next.js</title>
217: ```
218: 
219: ##### `default`
220: 
221: `title.default` can be used to provide a **fallback title** to child route segments that don't define a `title`.
222: 
223: ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx"
224: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
225: 
226: export const metadata: Metadata = {
227:   title: {
228:     default: 'Acme',
229:   },
230: }
231: ```
232: 
233: ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx"
234: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
235: 
236: export const metadata: Metadata = {}
237: 
238: // Output: <title>Acme</title>
239: ```
240: 
241: ##### `template`
242: 
243: `title.template` can be used to add a prefix or a suffix to `titles` defined in **child** route segments.
244: 
245: ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
246: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
247: 
248: export const metadata: Metadata = {
249:   title: {
250:     template: '%s | Acme',
251:     default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
252:   },
253: }
254: ```
255: 
256: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
257: export const metadata = {
258:   title: {
259:     template: '%s | Acme',
260:     default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
261:   },
262: }
263: ```
264: 
265: ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
266: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
267: 
268: export const metadata: Metadata = {
269:   title: 'About',
270: }
271: 
272: // Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
273: ```
274: 
275: ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
276: export const metadata = {
277:   title: 'About',
278: }
279: 
280: // Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
281: ```
282: 
283: > **Good to know**:
284: >
285: > - `title.template` applies to **child** route segments and **not** the segment it's defined in. This means:
286: >   - `title.default` is **required** when you add a `title.template`.
287: >   - `title.template` defined in `layout.js` will not apply to a `title` defined in a `page.js` of the same route segment.
288: >   - `title.template` defined in `page.js` has no effect because a page is always the terminating segment (it doesn't have any children route segments).
289: > - `title.template` has **no effect** if a route has not defined a `title` or `title.default`.
290: 
291: ##### `absolute`
292: 
293: `title.absolute` can be used to provide a title that **ignores** `title.template` set in parent segments.
294: 
295: ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
296: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
297: 
298: export const metadata: Metadata = {
299:   title: {
300:     template: '%s | Acme',
301:   },
302: }
303: ```
304: 
305: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
306: export const metadata = {
307:   title: {
308:     template: '%s | Acme',
309:   },
310: }
311: ```
312: 
313: ```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
314: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
315: 
316: export const metadata: Metadata = {
317:   title: {
318:     absolute: 'About',
319:   },
320: }
321: 
322: // Output: <title>About</title>
323: ```
324: 
325: ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
326: export const metadata = {
327:   title: {
328:     absolute: 'About',
329:   },
330: }
331: 
332: // Output: <title>About</title>
333: ```
334: 
335: > **Good to know**:
336: >
337: > - `layout.js`
338: >   - `title` (string) and `title.default` define the default title for child segments (that do not define their own `title`). It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
339: >   - `title.absolute` defines the default title for child segments. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
340: >   - `title.template` defines a new title template for child segments.
341: > - `page.js`
342: >   - If a page does not define its own title the closest parents resolved title will be used.
343: >   - `title` (string) defines the routes title. It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
344: >   - `title.absolute` defines the route title. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
345: >   - `title.template` has no effect in `page.js` because a page is always the terminating segment of a route.
346:

391: #### `metadataBase`
392: 
393: `metadataBase` is a convenience option to set a base URL prefix for `metadata` fields that require a fully qualified URL.
394: 
395: - `metadataBase` allows URL-based `metadata` fields defined in the **current route segment and below** to use a **relative path** instead of an otherwise required absolute URL.
396: - The field's relative path will be composed with `metadataBase` to form a fully qualified URL.
397: 
398: ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
399: export const metadata = {
400:   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
401:   alternates: {
402:     canonical: '/',
403:     languages: {
404:       'en-US': '/en-US',
405:       'de-DE': '/de-DE',
406:     },
407:   },
408:   openGraph: {
409:     images: '/og-image.png',
410:   },
411: }
412: ```
413: 
414: ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
415: <link rel="canonical" href="https://acme.com" />
416: <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en-US" href="https://acme.com/en-US" />
417: <link rel="alternate" hreflang="de-DE" href="https://acme.com/de-DE" />
418: <meta property="og:image" content="https://acme.com/og-image.png" />
419: ```
420: 
421: > **Good to know**:
422: >
423: > - `metadataBase` is typically set in root `app/layout.js` to apply to URL-based `metadata` fields across all routes.
424: > - When `generateMetadata` uses `'use cache'`, its return value must be serializable. `URL` instances are not supported by Cache Functions, so values such as `metadataBase` should be returned as strings (for example, `url.toString()`). See [`use cache` serialization requirements](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#serialization).
425: > - All URL-based `metadata` fields that require absolute URLs can be configured with a `metadataBase` option.
426: > - `metadataBase` can contain a subdomain e.g. `https://app.acme.com` or base path e.g. `https://acme.com/start/from/here`
427: > - If a `metadata` field provides an absolute URL, `metadataBase` will be ignored.
428: > - Using a relative path in a URL-based `metadata` field without configuring a `metadataBase` will cause a build error.
429: > - Next.js will normalize duplicate slashes between `metadataBase` (e.g. `https://acme.com/`) and a relative field (e.g. `/path`) to a single slash (e.g. `https://acme.com/path`)
430: 
431: #### URL Composition
432: 
433: URL composition favors developer intent over default directory traversal semantics.
434: 
435: - Trailing slashes between `metadataBase` and `metadata` fields are normalized.
436: - An "absolute" path in a `metadata` field (that typically would replace the whole URL path) is treated as a "relative" path (starting from the end of `metadataBase`).
437: 
438: For example, given the following `metadataBase`:
439: 
440: ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
441: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
442: 
443: export const metadata: Metadata = {
444:   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
445: }
446: ```
447: 
448: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
449: export const metadata = {
450:   metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
451: }
452: ```
453: 
454: Any `metadata` fields that inherit the above `metadataBase` and set their own value will be resolved as follows:
455: 
456: | `metadata` field                 | Resolved URL                     |
457: | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
458: | `/`                              | `https://acme.com`               |
459: | `./`                             | `https://acme.com`               |
460: | `payments`                       | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
461: | `/payments`                      | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
462: | `./payments`                     | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
463: | `../payments`                    | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
464: | `https://beta.acme.com/payments` | `https://beta.acme.com/payments` |
465:

1048: ### Types
1049: 
1050: You can add type safety to your metadata by using the `Metadata` type. If you are using the [built-in TypeScript plugin](/docs/app/api-reference/config/typescript) in your IDE, you do not need to manually add the type, but you can still explicitly add it if you want.
1051: 
1052: #### `metadata` object
1053: 
1054: ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1055: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1056: 
1057: export const metadata: Metadata = {
1058:   title: 'Next.js',
1059: }
1060: ```
1061: 
1062: #### `generateMetadata` function
1063: 
1064: ##### Regular function
1065: 
1066: ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1067: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1068: 
1069: export function generateMetadata(): Metadata {
1070:   return {
1071:     title: 'Next.js',
1072:   }
1073: }
1074: ```
1075: 
1076: ##### Async function
1077: 
1078: ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1079: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1080: 
1081: export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {
1082:   return {
1083:     title: 'Next.js',
1084:   }
1085: }
1086: ```
1087: 
1088: ##### With segment props
1089: 
1090: ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1091: import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1092: 
1093: type Props = {
1094:   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
1095:   searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
1096: }
1097: 
1098: export function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }: Props): Metadata {
1099:   return {
1100:     title: 'Next.js',
1101:   }
1102: }
1103: 
1104: export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
1105: ```
1106: 
1107: ##### With parent metadata
1108: 
1109: ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1110: import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
1111: 
1112: export async function generateMetadata(
1113:   { params, searchParams }: Props,
1114:   parent: ResolvingMetadata
1115: ): Promise<Metadata> {
1116:   return {
1117:     title: 'Next.js',
1118:   }
1119: }
1120: ```

1138: | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1139: | `<meta http-equiv="...">`     | Use appropriate HTTP Headers via [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect), [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#nextresponse), [Security Headers](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers) |
1140: | `<base>`                      | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
1141: | `<noscript>`                  | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
1142: | `<style>`                     | Learn more about [styling in Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/css).                                                                                                                                                                        |
1143: | `<script>`                    | Learn more about [using scripts](/docs/app/guides/scripts).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
1144: | `<link rel="stylesheet" />`   | `import` stylesheets directly in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
1145: | `<link rel="preload" />`      | Use [ReactDOM preload method](#link-relpreload)                                                                                                                                                                                              |
1146: | `<link rel="preconnect" />`   | Use [ReactDOM preconnect method](#link-relpreconnect)                                                                                                                                                                                        |
1147: | `<link rel="dns-prefetch" />` | Use [ReactDOM prefetchDNS method](#link-reldns-prefetch)                                                                                                                                                                                     |

1149: ### Resource hints
1150: 
1151: The `<link>` element has a number of `rel` keywords that can be used to hint to the browser that an external resource is likely to be needed. The browser uses this information to apply preloading optimizations depending on the keyword.
1152: 
1153: While the Metadata API doesn't directly support these hints, you can use new [`ReactDOM` methods](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/26237) to safely insert them into the `<head>` of the document.
1154: 
1155: ```tsx filename="app/preload-resources.tsx" switcher
1156: 'use client'
1157: 
1158: import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
1159: 
1160: export function PreloadResources() {
1161:   ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
1162:   ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
1163:   ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
1164: 
1165:   return '...'
1166: }
1167: ```
1168: 
1169: ```jsx filename="app/preload-resources.js" switcher
1170: 'use client'
1171: 
1172: import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
1173: 
1174: export function PreloadResources() {
1175:   ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
1176:   ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
1177:   ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
1178: 
1179:   return '...'
1180: }
1181: ```
1182: 
1183: #### `<link rel="preload">`
1184: 
1185: Start loading a resource early in the page rendering (browser) lifecycle. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preload).
1186: 
1187: ```tsx
1188: ReactDOM.preload(href: string, options: { as: string })
1189: ```
1190: 
1191: ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1192: <link rel="preload" href="..." as="..." />
1193: ```
1194: 
1195: ##### `<link rel="preconnect">`
1196: 
1197: Preemptively initiate a connection to an origin. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preconnect).
1198: 
1199: ```tsx
1200: ReactDOM.preconnect(href: string, options?: { crossOrigin?: string })
1201: ```
1202: 
1203: ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1204: <link rel="preconnect" href="..." crossorigin />
1205: ```
1206: 
1207: #### `<link rel="dns-prefetch">`
1208: 
1209: Attempt to resolve a domain name before resources get requested. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/dns-prefetch).
1210: 
1211: ```tsx
1212: ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(href: string)
1213: ```
1214: 
1215: ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1216: <link rel="dns-prefetch" href="..." />
1217: ```
1218: 
1219: > **Good to know**:
1220: >
1221: > - These methods are currently only supported in Client Components, which are still Server Side Rendered on initial page load.
1222: > - Next.js in-built features such as `next/font`, `next/image` and `next/script` automatically handle relevant resource hints.
1223: 
1224: ## Behavior
1225: 
1226: ### Default Fields
1227: 
1228: There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
1229: 
1230: - The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
1231: - The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
1232: 
1233: ```html
1234: <meta charset="utf-8" />
1235: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
1236: ```
1237: 
1238: > **Good to know**: You can overwrite the default [`viewport`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#viewport) meta tag.
1239: 
1240: ### Streaming metadata
1241: 
1242: Streaming metadata allows Next.js to render and send the initial UI to the browser, without waiting for `generateMetadata` to complete.
1243: 
1244: When `generateMetadata` resolves, the resulting metadata tags are appended to the `<body>` tag. We have verified that metadata is interpreted correctly by bots that execute JavaScript and inspect the full DOM (e.g. `Googlebot`).
1245: 
1246: For **HTML-limited bots** that can’t execute JavaScript (e.g. `facebookexternalhit`), metadata continues to block page rendering. The resulting metadata will be available in the `<head>` tag.
1247: 
1248: Next.js automatically detects **HTML-limited bots** by looking at the User Agent header. You can use the [`htmlLimitedBots`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/htmlLimitedBots) option in your Next.js config file to override the default [User Agent list](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/html-bots.ts).
1249: 
1250: To fully disable streaming metadata:
1251: 
1252: ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
1253: import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
1254: 
1255: const config: NextConfig = {
1256:   htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
1257: }
1258: 
1259: export default config
1260: ```
1261: 
1262: ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
1263: module.exports = {
1264:   htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
1265: }
1266: ```
1267: 
1268: Streaming metadata improves perceived performance by reducing [TTFB](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Time_to_first_byte) and can help lowering [LCP](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Largest_contentful_paint) time.
1269: 
1270: Overriding `htmlLimitedBots` could lead to longer response times. Streaming metadata is an advanced feature, and the default should be sufficient for most cases.
1271: 
1272: ### With Cache Components
1273: 
1274: When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `generateMetadata` follows the same rules as other components. If metadata accesses runtime data (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `params`, `searchParams`) or performs uncached data fetching, it defers to request time.
1275: 
1276: How Next.js handles this depends on the rest of your page:
1277: 
1278: - **If other parts also defer to request time**: Prerendering generates a static shell, and metadata streams in with other deferred content.
1279: - **If the page or layout is otherwise fully prerenderable**: Next.js requires an explicit choice: cache the data if possible, or signal that deferred rendering is intentional.
1280: 
1281: Streaming metadata at runtime while the rest of the page is fully prerenderable is not common. To ensure this behavior is intentional, an error is raised indicating which page or layout needs to be handled.
1282: 
1283: To resolve this, you have two options. If metadata depends on external data but not runtime data, use `use cache`:
1284: 
1285: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={2}
1286: export async function generateMetadata() {
1287:   'use cache'
1288:   const { title, description } = await db.query('site-metadata')
1289:   return { title, description }
1290: }
1291: ```
1292: 
1293: If metadata genuinely requires runtime data, add a dynamic marker component to your page:
1294: 
1295: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={11-14,19,31}
1296: import { Suspense } from 'react'
1297: import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
1298: import { connection } from 'next/server'
1299: 
1300: export async function generateMetadata() {
1301:   const token = (await cookies()).get('token')?.value
1302:   // ... use token to fetch personalized metadata
1303:   return { title: 'Personalized Title' }
1304: }
1305: 
1306: const Connection = async () => {
1307:   await connection()
1308:   return null
1309: }
1310: 
1311: async function DynamicMarker() {
1312:   return (
1313:     <Suspense>
1314:       <Connection />
1315:     </Suspense>
1316:   )
1317: }
1318: 
1319: export default function Page() {
1320:   // DO NOT place await connection() here
1321:   // doing so prevents the article tag content from
1322:   // being included in the static shell
1323:   return (
1324:     <>
1325:       <article>Static content</article>
1326:       <DynamicMarker />
1327:     </>
1328:   )
1329: }
1330: ```
1331: 
1332: The `DynamicMarker` component renders nothing but tells Next.js the page has intentional dynamic content. By wrapping it in Suspense, the static content still prerenders normally.
1333: 
1334: See [Next.js encountered runtime data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) and [Next.js encountered uncached data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-dynamic) for full fix options and trade-offs.
1335: 
1336: ### Ordering
1337: 
1338: Metadata is evaluated in order, starting from the root segment down to the segment closest to the final `page.js` segment. For example:
1339: 
1340: 1. `app/layout.tsx` (Root Layout)
1341: 2. `app/blog/layout.tsx` (Nested Blog Layout)
1342: 3. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (Blog Page)
1343: 
1344: ### Merging
1345: 
1346: Following the [evaluation order](#ordering), Metadata objects exported from multiple segments in the same route are **shallowly** merged together to form the final metadata output of a route. Duplicate keys are **replaced** based on their ordering.
1347: 
1348: This means metadata with nested fields such as [`openGraph`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#opengraph) and [`robots`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#robots) that are defined in an earlier segment are **overwritten** by the last segment to define them.
1349: 
1350: #### Overwriting fields
1351: 
1352: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
1353: export const metadata = {
1354:   title: 'Acme',
1355:   openGraph: {
1356:     title: 'Acme',
1357:     description: 'Acme is a...',
1358:   },
1359: }
1360: ```
1361: 
1362: ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js"
1363: export const metadata = {
1364:   title: 'Blog',
1365:   openGraph: {
1366:     title: 'Blog',
1367:   },
1368: }
1369: 
1370: // Output:
1371: // <title>Blog</title>
1372: // <meta property="og:title" content="Blog" />
1373: ```
1374: 
1375: In the example above:
1376: 
1377: - `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/blog/page.js`.
1378: - All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **replaced** in `app/blog/page.js` because `app/blog/page.js` sets `openGraph` metadata. Note the absence of `openGraph.description`.
1379: 
1380: If you'd like to share some nested fields between segments while overwriting others, you can pull them out into a separate variable:
1381: 
1382: ```jsx filename="app/shared-metadata.js"
1383: export const openGraphImage = { images: ['http://...'] }
1384: ```
1385: 
1386: ```jsx filename="app/page.js"
1387: import { openGraphImage } from './shared-metadata'
1388: 
1389: export const metadata = {
1390:   openGraph: {
1391:     ...openGraphImage,
1392:     title: 'Home',
1393:   },
1394: }
1395: ```
1396: 
1397: ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
1398: import { openGraphImage } from '../shared-metadata'
1399: 
1400: export const metadata = {
1401:   openGraph: {
1402:     ...openGraphImage,
1403:     title: 'About',
1404:   },
1405: }
1406: ```
1407: 
1408: In the example above, the OG image is shared between `app/layout.js` and `app/about/page.js` while the titles are different.
1409: 
1410: #### Inheriting fields
1411: 
1412: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
1413: export const metadata = {
1414:   title: 'Acme',
1415:   openGraph: {
1416:     title: 'Acme',
1417:     description: 'Acme is a...',
1418:   },
1419: }
1420: ```
1421: 
1422: ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
1423: export const metadata = {
1424:   title: 'About',
1425: }
1426: 
1427: // Output:
1428: // <title>About</title>
1429: // <meta property="og:title" content="Acme" />
1430: // <meta property="og:description" content="Acme is a..." />
1431: ```
1432: 
1433: **Notes**
1434: 
1435: - `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/about/page.js`.
1436: - All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **inherited** in `app/about/page.js` because `app/about/page.js` doesn't set `openGraph` metadata.
1437:

1439: 
1440: | Version   | Changes                                                                                                                                                 |
1441: | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

1444: | `v13.2.0` | `metadata` and `generateMetadata` introduced.                                                                                                           |

6: The `opengraph-image` and `twitter-image` file conventions allow you to set Open Graph and Twitter images for a route segment.

16: 
17: Use an image file to set a route segment's shared image by placing an `opengraph-image` or `twitter-image` image file in the segment.
18: 
19: Next.js will evaluate the file and automatically add the appropriate tags to your app's `<head>` element.

# SwapDesk Frontend

The frontend dashboard for **SwapDesk** — autonomous middleware between a e-commerce helpdesk and its commerce stack that resolves exchanges, returns, and refunds safely. It is an idempotent, policy-aware agent runtime.

Built as a self-contained Next.js app with **client-side demo state** — no backend is required to run or demo it.

## Tech Stack

- **Next.js 16.4.0** (App Router, Turbopack, `cacheComponents` + `partialPrefetching` enabled)
- **React 19** with Server & Client Components
- **TypeScript** (strict), path alias `@/*` → `./src/*`
- **Tailwind CSS v4** (CSS-first theme tokens in `app/globals.css`)
- **lucide-react** icons
- **sonner** toasts
- Fonts via `next/font/google`: **Bricolage Grotesque** (display), **Plus Jakarta Sans** (body), **Geist Mono** (technical/mono)

## Getting Started

```bash
npm install      # install dependencies
npm run dev      # start the development server (http://localhost:3000)
```

Other scripts:

| Script          | Description                                    |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run build` | Production build (static + partial prerender)  |
| `npm run start` | Serve the production build                     |
| `npm run lint`  | ESLint (flat config)                           |

## Environment Variables

| Variable                 | Default                             | Purpose                                                                |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`   | `https://swapdesk.vercel.app`       | Canonical origin used for `metadataBase`, canonical URLs, sitemap, robots. Override when deploying. |

## Project Structure

```
app/
├── layout.tsx              # Root layout, global <head> metadata, fonts, SwapDeskProvider, Toaster
├── page.tsx                # Server entry → renders <MissionControl />
├── mission-control.tsx     # "Mission Control" home (client) — metrics + live queue
├── inbox/page.tsx          # Full ticket inbox (static demo data)
├── inventory/              # Live stock + reservations (client; stock reacts to simulations)
│   ├── layout.tsx          #   metadata
│   └── page.tsx
├── database/layout.tsx     # Schema view (metadata)
├── integrations/           # Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify Inbox, Gorgias)
│   ├── layout.tsx          #   metadata
│   └── page.tsx
├── settings/layout.tsx     # Agent autonomy/guardrail settings (metadata)
├── simulate/page.tsx       # Customer Simulation — inject a ticket into the queue
├── ticket/[id]/page.tsx    # Ticket execution detail (Suspense split; see below)
├── robots.ts               # /robots.txt
├── sitemap.ts              # /sitemap.xml
├── opengraph-image.tsx     # Generated OG image (ImageResponse)
├── twitter-image.tsx       # Re-exports from opengraph-image
└── globals.css             # Theme tokens + utilities (panel, glass, pulse-dot, num, rise)

src/
├── components/
│   ├── AppShell.tsx                # Sidebar + top bar + mobile bottom nav, "Simulate Ticket" button
│   └── CustomerSimulationWidget.tsx
├── lib/
│   ├── seo.ts                      # SITE_* constants + pageMetadata() helper
│   └── utils.ts                    # cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge)
└── store/
    └── swapdesk.tsx                # Global demo state + SwapDeskProvider
```

## Demo Flow

Everything is driven by a client-side store — no network calls.

1. Click **Simulate Ticket** (top bar) or open **Customer Simulation** (`/simulate`), type a complaint, and submit.
2. The store appends a ticket with status `Agent Processing` (`INTAKE` / `ROUTING` actions).
3. It appears instantly in **Mission Control** and the **Inbox**, filterable by status.
4. Open any ticket to inspect its execution timeline, actions, and SKU reservation.
5. **Simulate Ticket** also decrements stock for `AJ4-MIL-43` (5 → 4) — visible on `/inventory`.
6. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) clears tickets and restores stock.

## State Management

`src/store/swapdesk.tsx` exposes a `SwapDeskProvider` (mounted in `app/layout.tsx`) plus a `useSwapDesk()` hook:

```ts
const { tickets, inventory, simulateTicket, submitCustomerTicket, resetMockData, getTicket } =
  useSwapDesk();
```

- `TicketStatus` = `"resolved" | "escalated" | "processing"`
- `simulateTicket(): Ticket` — prepends `TCK-9045+` resolved ticket, decrements `AJ4-MIL-43` stock.
- `submitCustomerTicket(message): Ticket` — prepends a `processing` ticket with your message.
- `resetMockData()` — wipes tickets, restores initial inventory.
- `getTicket(id)` — look up a single ticket.

## Routes

| Route                 | Page                    | Type            | Notes                              |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `/`                   | Mission Control         | server + client | metrics + live queue, filter       |
| `/inbox`              | Inbox                   | server          | static ticket list                 |
| `/inventory`          | Inventory               | server layout + client page | stock reacts to simulations |
| `/database`           | Database Schema         | server          |                                    |
| `/integrations`       | Integrations            | server layout + client page | webhook toggle + URL copy  |
| `/settings`           | Agent Settings          | server          |                                    |
| `/simulate`           | Customer Simulation     | server          | `CustomerSimulationWidget`         |
| `/ticket/[id]`        | Ticket Execution        | client          | Partial Prerender (Suspense)       |
| `/robots.txt`         | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
| `/sitemap.xml`        | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
| `/opengraph-image`    | —                       | image route     | generated 1200×630 PNG             |
| `/twitter-image`      | —                       | image route     | re-export of opengraph-image       |

> **Turbopack dynamic route note:** `/ticket/[id]` must pre-render its HTML shell at build time. Client hooks that need URL data (`useParams`, `usePathname`) therefore live behind `<Suspense>` and out of the static shell. See `app/ticket/[id]/page.tsx`.

## Design System

Theme tokens live in `app/globals.css` as CSS variables and Tailwind v4 `@theme` mappings:

- Colors: `--card: #111113`, `--border: #222225`, `--color-success` (green), `--color-primary`, `--color-warning`, `--color-danger`, `--color-hairline`
- Type: `font-display` (`--font-bricolage`), `font-sans` (`--font-jakarta`), `font-mono` (`--font-geist-mono`)
- Utilities: `panel` (card), `glass` (frosted nav), `pulse-dot`, `num` (tabular numerals), `rise` (entry animation)

> **Guideline:** keep server-rendered pages static where possible and Textomove interactivity into client components. Do not introduce a visual redesign — extend the existing token system.

## SEO

Add full metadata to every segment:

- Root (`app/layout.tsx`): `metadataBase`, titles with `template: "%s · SwapDesk"`, description, keywords, `<viewport>` (themeColor), OpenGraph + Twitter cards, `robots`, `applicationName`, authors, category.
- Per page: use the `pageMetadata({ title, description, path })` helper from `src/lib/seo.ts` (marked `Export const metadata`).
- Images: `app/opengraph-image.tsx` generates a themed 1200×630 card with `ImageResponse`; `app/twitter-image.tsx` re-exports it.
- Crawling: `app/robots.ts` and `app/sitemap.ts` reflect the remaining routes.

Set the title without the site name suffix — the root template appends ` · SwapDesk`.

## Deploy

Deploy on Vercel (or any Node host running `npm run build && npm run start`):

```bash
npm run build
npm run start
```

Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to your production origin so canonical URLs, sitemap, and robots are correct.

1: # SwapDesk
2: 
3: SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop. A customer asks for a different size, and the backend checks policy and stock, holds a replacement, creates a return and a mock label, then verifies the saved state. Every request ends in one of four outcomes: exchange arranged, clarification required, policy denial, or human escalation. All data is synthetic. There are no payments, shipments, or real customers.
4: 
5: This repo holds the backend. It is a neatHack project, currently at Slice 5 of 7 (FastAPI for the frontend team). The demo does not exist yet.
6: 
7: ## Features
8: 
9: Implemented:
10: 
11: - Atomic stock reservation with no oversell, safe under concurrent writers
12: - Idempotent operations: same key plus same payload returns the saved result, same key plus different payload is rejected
13: - Policy enforcement in the backend: delivered status, 30-day window, final sale excluded
14: - One active exchange per order item, across cases
15: - Append-only action journal for every committed or duplicate-routed operation
16: - Full mock exchange: return and label creation, hold release, cancel, escalation, case progress, read-only recovery handoff
17: - Controlled failure injection (demo-only `faults` module) with same-key recovery
18: - Deterministic pytest suite (34 tests, no network, no model)
19: - Independent checker plus frozen 30-case benchmark (`eval/cases_v1.json`, 8 holdouts, 42 runs)
20: - One LangGraph tool-using agent (`langchain.agents.create_agent`, Gemini): curated tools, bounded loop, file-backed checkpoints, DB-derived outcomes, template replies
21: - neatlogs wiring (workflow/tool spans, flush): local capture without a key, export with one
22: 
23: Planned, not built: FastAPI routes, business model in cfo.ai.
24: 
25: ## Installation
26: 
27: Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
28: 
29: ```bash
30: git clone https://github.com/adr1en360/SwapDesk.git
31: cd SwapDesk
32: uv sync
33: ```
34: 
35: ## Usage
36: 
37: Run the test suite:
38: 
39: ```bash
40: uv run pytest -q
41: ```
42: 
43: Reserve a replacement from a scratch database:
44: 
45: ```bash
46: uv run python -c "
47: from swapdesk.db import connect, init_db
48: from swapdesk.fixtures import load_fixtures
49: from swapdesk.operations import reserve_replacement
50: 
51: conn = connect('scratch.db')
52: init_db(conn)
53: load_fixtures(conn)
54: conn.close()
55: 
56: result = reserve_replacement(
57:     'scratch.db', case_id='CASE-DEMO', run_id='RUN-DEMO', op_key='OP-DEMO',
58:     order_id='ORD-1001', order_item_id='ITEM-01', size='42')
59: print(result)
60: "
61: ```
62: 
63: Check what a previous operation did:
64: 
65: ```bash
66: uv run python -c "
67: from swapdesk.operations import get_operation_status
68: print(get_operation_status('scratch.db', 'OP-DEMO'))
69: "
70: ```
71: 
72: Delete `scratch.db` when done. It is git-ignored.

74: ## Studio verification
75: 
76: Full runbook with evidence: [docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md).
77: 
78: Two graphs share one architecture (`prepare` → nested `agent` subgraph → `verify`), defined in `src/swapdesk/agent/studio_flow.py` and served from `langgraph.json`:
79: 
80: ```bash
81: uv run langgraph dev
82: ```
83: 
84: Open Studio at `https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8123` (override the port with `--port`). You will see two assistants:
85: 
86: - **`swapdesk_offline` (default).** A scripted model replays tool calls against the real backend. Zero model requests. This proves the wiring, never Gemini's decisions; the evidence panel labels every offline run accordingly.
87: - **`swapdesk_live` (opt-in).** Budget-capped Gemini. Each run needs an explicit request budget plus `SWAPDESK_MODEL` and `GEMINI_API_KEY`; anything missing fails loudly before any model call. Nothing live runs until you explicitly invoke a budgeted smoke test.

The `verify` node shows the outcome derived from persisted state, the database evidence (exchanges, operations, case state), and the rendered customer reply.
105: 
106: Rules the graphs enforce: one isolated database per case under `studio_data/` (git-ignored); reusing a case id without `"resume": true` errors instead of resetting; resume preserves the case, operation keys, and thread state. Thread persistence comes from the serving platform, so the served graphs compile without a custom checkpointer (the server rejects one); tests pass an explicit file saver to the same builders. The request cap counts every model request including retries and refuses past the budget; the recursion limit alone is not a request budget. Demo scenarios use fresh `DEMO-*` cases only and never load the frozen benchmark, so holdouts stay out of demo tuning. Opening Studio, importing the graphs, and running offline tests make zero model requests.
107: 
108: ## API for frontend teammates
109: 
110: ```bash
111: uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app
112: ```
113: 
114: Interactive docs at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (generated from the implementation, always in sync). The demo database is `swapdesk.db` (override with `SWAPDESK_DB`); restarting reuses it, fixtures seed once.
115: 
116: | Method & route | What it does |
117: |---|---|
118: | `POST /v1/tickets` | Submit a ticket, run it to a verified outcome (201) |
119: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}` | Verified status, outcome, reply, run ids (404 unknown) |
120: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline` | Sanitized action/journal events (404 unknown) |
121: | `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue` | Continue with message/consent (404 unknown, 422 uncontinuable) |
122: | `GET /v1/fixtures` | Synthetic orders, items, and policy for dropdowns |
123: | `POST /v1/demo/faults` | Demo-only: arm one failure on an operation key |
124: | `DELETE /v1/demo/faults` | Demo-only: disarm all failures |
125: | `GET /v1/health` | Liveness probe |
126: 
127: Outcomes (`arranged`, `clarification`, `denial`, `escalation`) always return 200 with an `outcome` field — a denial is an answer, not an error. Only malformed requests (422), unknown cases (404), and unexpected failures (500, generic message) are HTTP errors.

input.content:
# SwapDesk

SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop. A customer asks for a different size, and the system checks policy and stock, holds a replacement, creates a return and a mock label, then verifies the saved state. Every request ends in one of four outcomes: **exchange arranged**, **clarification required**, **policy denial**, or **human escalation**.

All data is synthetic. There are no payments, shipments, or real customers. This is a neatHack project built by a team of four.

## Repository layout

```text
frontend/          Next.js dashboard — standalone client-side demo (no backend required)
src/swapdesk/      Python backend package — FastAPI, SQLite, LangGraph agent
eval/              Frozen benchmark, deterministic checker, and run harness
tests/             Deterministic pytest suite (no network, no model)
docs/              Build plan, runbooks, evidence, and business deliverables
hackathon.md       Slice-by-slice build log and team conventions
```

## The two halves

- **Backend** (`src/swapdesk/`) — the agent runtime. Policy checks, atomic stock reservation, idempotent operations, an append-only action journal, a LangGraph tool-using agent, and a FastAPI surface for frontend integration. Deterministic and network-free to test.
- **Frontend** (`frontend/`) — the ops dashboard (Mission Control, Inbox, Inventory, Integrations, Customer Simulation, ticket detail). It is a **self-contained client-side demo** powered by a mock store — it demos the SwapDesk experience without calling the live API. Its own README lives at [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md).

---

## Backend

### Features

- Atomic stock reservation with no oversell, safe under concurrent writers.
- Idempotent operations: same key plus same payload returns the saved result; same key plus different payload is rejected.
- Policy enforcement: delivered status, 30-day return window, final-sale excluded.
- One active exchange per order item, across cases.
- Append-only action journal for every committed or duplicate-routed operation.
- Full mock exchange lifecycle: reserve → return → label → arrange, plus hold release, cancel, escalation, cleanup recovery, and a read-only verification handoff.
- Demo-only failure injection (`faults.py`) with same-key recovery.
- A LangGraph tool-using agent (`langchain.agents.create_agent`, Gemini or a LiteLLM proxy): curated tools, bounded loop, budget-capped requests, file-backed checkpoints, database-derived outcomes, template replies.
- neatlogs wiring (workflow/tool spans, local capture without a key, export with one).

### Installation

Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/adr1en360/SwapDesk.git
cd SwapDesk
uv sync
```

### Test

```bash
uv run pytest -q
```

The suite is deterministic — no network, no model keys, no LLM judge.

### Run the API

```bash
uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app
```

Interactive docs at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (generated from the implementation, always in sync). The demo database is `swapdesk.db` (override with `SWAPDESK_DB`); restarting reuses it, fixtures seed once.

| Method & route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/tickets` | Submit a ticket and run it to a verified outcome (201) |
| `GET /v1/cases/{id}` | Verified status, outcome, reply, run ids (404 unknown) |
| `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline` | Sanitized action/journal events (404 unknown) |
| `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue` | Continue with message/consent (404 unknown, 422 uncontinuable) |
| `GET /v1/fixtures` | Synthetic orders, items, and policy for dropdowns |
| `POST /v1/demo/faults` | Demo-only: arm one failure on an operation key |
| `DELETE /v1/demo/faults` | Demo-only: disarm all failures |
| `GET /v1/health` | Liveness probe |

Outcomes (`arranged`, `clarification`, `denial`, `escalation`) always return 200 with an `outcome` field — a denial is an answer, not an error. Only malformed requests (422), unknown cases (404), and unexpected failures (500, generic message) are HTTP errors.

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/tickets \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'

curl localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx
curl localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx/timeline
curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/cases/CASE-xxx/continue \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"consent_size":"42","order_id":"ORD-1005","order_item_id":"ITEM-06","size":"43"}'
```

No authentication: this is a local mock. Execution runs synchronously per request, so status reads are never blocked.

### Configuring the agent

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have (`.env` is git-ignored; never commit it):

- `GEMINI_API_KEY` — direct Gemini access (no `LITELLM_API_KEY`).
- `LITELLM_API_KEY` — enables the hackathon LiteLLM proxy instead; `SWAPDESK_MODEL` then picks from `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` (default `claude-haiku`). Override the endpoint with `LITELLM_BASE_URL`.
- `SWAPDESK_MODEL` — Gemini model id when using Gemini directly (default `gemini-3.8-flash`).
- `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` + `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` — neatlogs telemetry export; local-only capture works without them.

Live model calls and telemetry export need working egress to the upstream APIs; where the network blocks them, the deterministic suites still pass.

### Inspecting the agent in LangGraph Studio

Two graphs share one architecture (`prepare` → nested `agent` subgraph → `verify`), defined in `src/swapdesk/agent/studio_flow.py` and served from `langgraph.json`:

```bash
uv run langgraph dev
```

Open Studio at `https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8123`. Two assistants are registered:

- **`swapdesk_offline` (default).** A scripted model replays tool calls against the real backend — zero model requests. Proves the wiring, never Gemini's decisions.
- **`swapdesk_live` (opt-in).** Budget-capped Gemini. Needs `SWAPDESK_MODEL` plus `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or the LiteLLM pair) and a per-run budget; anything missing fails loudly before any model call.

Full runbook with evidence: [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md).

## Frontend

A Next.js 16 (Turbopack) App Router dashboard with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4.

### Run it

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
```

Other scripts: `npm run build` (production build), `npm run start`, `npm run lint`.

### Pages and demo flow

| Route | Page | What it demos |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | Mission Control | Agent metrics + live execution queue |
| `/inbox` | Inbox | Sample ticket stream |
| `/inventory` | Inventory | Stock levels that react to simulations |
| `/database` | Database Schema | Tables the agent reads/writes |
| `/integrations` | Integrations | Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify, Gorgias) |
| `/settings` | Agent Settings | Autonomy/guardrail config UI |
| `/simulate` | Customer Simulation | Inject a customer complaint into the queue |
| `/ticket/[id]` | Ticket Execution | Per-ticket action timeline |

The demo runs entirely on a client-side store (`frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`). **Simulate Ticket** prepends a resolved ticket and decrements `AJ4-MIL-43` stock; **Customer Simulation** injects a ticket with an `Agent Processing` status; **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) restores the initial state. Dashboard labels reflect the actual mock state — completion rate is computed from the queue, and cost shows "Demo Mode".

SEO is configured across all routes (per-page metadata, generated Open Graph/Twitter images, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`). See [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md) and [`frontend/setup.md`](frontend/setup.md) for details.

## Evaluation and evidence

- `eval/cases_v1.json` — frozen 30-case benchmark (`benchmark-v1`, 8 holdouts) covering arrangement, denial, clarification, and escalation, with seeded fault schedules.
- `eval/driver.py` — deterministic reference driver (not the agent) that exercises the cases.
- `eval/harness.py` + `eval/run.py` — isolated database per run; results committed to `eval/results/v1.json`.
- `src/swapdesk/checker.py` — deterministic per-outcome checks and global invariants, no LLM judge.
- `docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md` — a controlled live BEFORE/AFTER comparison of the D1 final-sale denial evidence path.

## Documentation

| Doc | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`docs/build-plan.md`](docs/build-plan.md) | Full build plan (spec, not evidence) |
| [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md) | LangGraph Studio runbook with evidence |
| [`docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md`](docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md) | Runner/harness evidence walk-through |
| [`docs/business/`](docs/business/) | Business plan (MD/PDF) and financial model (XLSX) — figures are assumptions, not observed facts |
| [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md) | Slice-by-slice build log and conventions |

## Contributing

- Backend owns `src/swapdesk/` and `tests/`. Frontend owns `frontend/`.
- Keep tests deterministic; business logic stays callable without HTTP or a model.
- Record each slice in `hackathon.md` with the exact commands run and pass/fail counts.
- Never commit `.env`, databases, or real customer data. `.env.example` carries key names only.

## License
